Versus  STATE OF M.P THROUGH P.S. STATION ROAD RATLAM, DIST.
 RATLAM (M.P.)
Appearance:
Shri Vikas Rathi, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Tarun Pagare, learned Govt. Advocate for the respo  ShriShadab Khan, learned counsel for the respondent [OB  ORDER Heard and perused the record.

This is first bail application filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of Cr.P.C, 1973) for grant of bail during trial relating to Crime No.995/2024 dated (not mentioned), registered at Police Station-Station Road, District-Ratlam for the offence under Sections 406, 420, 34 & 409 of IPC.

The applicant is in custody since 10.11.2024.
2.
As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant has taken Rs.59.90 lakhs from the complainants for business purpose and for investment.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present crime.
It is further submitted that in the present case, the complainants are relatives to each other.
As per allegation, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9714 2 MCRC-11401-2025 the applicant has taken Rs.59.90 lakhs from the complainants for business purpose and for investment.
However, he has taken Rs.18,00,000/- in his account.
He is ready to deposit of Rs.18,00,000/- in three easy installments.

The applicant is in jail since 10.11.2024 i.e.

sentences.text: almost five months and he has no criminal antecedents.
Conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Under these circumstances, counsel prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the State as well counsel for objector have opposed the application and submitted that the applicant has taken Rs.1,12,00,000/-.
However, counsel for State has fairly admitted that the applicant is having no criminal record.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

6. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the rival submissions of the counsel for the parties, proposal made by the applicant, custody period of the applicant, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail subject to deposit Rs.6,00,000/- (either by the applicant or any other person on his behalf before the trial Court ) as well as on his/her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety to the satisfaction of the trial court for securing his/her presence before the said Court on all the dates of hearing fixed in this regard during trial.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
8.

It is made clear that after being enlarged on bail, the applicant shall deposit the remaining amount of Rs.12,00,000/- in two installments i.e. first installment of Rs.6,00,000/-shall be deposited within further four months from the date of his release and second installment of Rs.6,00,000/- shall be deposited NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9714 3 MCRC-11401-2025 thereafter in further four months.
In case of failure to to aforesaid, this bail order shall cancelled automatically without further reference to this Court.

9. This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified copy as per rules.
